title: The daemon resolves host context for human migration reverts
description: Fourth producer child of task-78eedd8ebc2b43c581ac21ea28648a9a (logical producer2), governor-directed re-slice19:10Z. At local0737 and ownerorigin4253, no non-test migrateDown: configuration exists. async-entries.ts139/322 spreads optional options.migrateDown; migrate-down-command.ts139–146 refuses MIGRATE_DOWN_UNCONFIGURED without host databaseUrl/workspace/projectRoot. Command537 and real revert engine are DONE; DO NOT republish kind/rebuild revert. Forward sibling2db owns reusable per-project/environment host-context resolver; depend on it instead of creating a second secret-resolution policy. Resolve request environment freshly, not one daemon-wide static URL incorrectly reused for every environment. Preserve default unconfigured refusal where evidence absent. Parent78 is browser/live proof consumer.
definitionOfDone: Default production daemon composition provides existing migrate-down command with host-resolved projectRoot/workspace and database context for exactly the admitted request environment. Test actual dispatch through default composition, not an isolated entry constructed with hardcoded databaseUrl; two environments prove isolation.

Unconfigured/missing/unreadable host context refuses MIGRATE_DOWN_UNCONFIGURED or the existing precise environment resolver code at its real layer before engine reads or writes. No fallback to arbitrary inherited DATABASE_URL, no browser-supplied URL/root/workspace, no secret-containing diagnostic.

Preserve HUMAN/operator-only async fence, HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS and MCP exclusion. Unauthorized real dispatch is rejected with code+layer before resolver/decrypt/engine effects; no new roster entries or authority widening. Authorized path reaches existing revertLastBatch and names the APPLIED request batch.

Live disposable-PostgreSQL arm through production composition applies two batches via shipped forward edge, reverts named last batch, asserts earlier schema remains and reverted schema disappears, then reads REVERTED receipt. Backup failure/not-last-batch/replay/concurrent revert preserve engine guarantees and unchanged schema where refused; no automatic restore.

Teardown every process/container/temp tree in finally on all outcomes; no connection value, SQL, password, derived credential value or tool banner in log/evidence. Fresh focused daemon tests/typecheck and named broader gates have nonzero counts; parent78 consumes wiring. Physical .js bridges for new runtime entrypoints.
taskRails: Reuse sibling2db host context and existing revert engine/fence. Production database values never enter browser or durable payload.
Do not overwrite whole shared registry files. Coordinate explicit paths and re-read owner-origin changes after reconciliation.

STEP 2 — THE SEAM IS PER-REQUEST. One file, `apps/daemon/src/deployment/migrate-down-command.ts`, 137 -> 160 lines (cap 250, fine).

(a) EXPORTED `MigrateDownHostContext` beside the options it belongs to — `{ databaseUrl, projectRoot, workspace }`, all THREE REQUIRED strings. Required, not optional, is the point: the three are host authority for ONE environment and are resolved together or not at all, so a half-answer cannot type-check its way past the fence.

(b) ON `MigrateDownCommandOptions`: the three optional strings are GONE and REPLACED by one optional resolver
```ts
readonly hostContext?: (environment: string) => MigrateDownHostContext | null;
```
Replaced, not added alongside — keeping the strings would leave two ways to configure the same thing and a silent precedence question, exactly as the plan says.

(c) THE CALL SITE — and here is the ONE PLACE I DEVIATED FROM THE STEP TEXT, deliberately, because the step's line-order premise is stale (measured and recorded in step 1's note).
The step says "call it with `identity.environment` — already in scope from :93". **It is not.** At HEAD `migrationCommandIdentity` is computed AFTER the config read, at :106, under a 7-line comment (:95-101) that explains WHY: `migrationCommandIdentity` itself refuses `MIGRATE_DOWN_TARGET_INVALID` / `MIGRATE_DOWN_PROJECT_MISMATCH` / `MIGRATE_DOWN_REQUEST_INVALID`, and on a daemon with nothing composed *"the operator's target is fine, so refusing it as MIGRATE_DOWN_TARGET_INVALID would be a substantively untrue reason for a true refusal."* Calling identity first unconditionally would break that.

So the check is SPLIT in two, which preserves both invariants at once:
```ts
const resolveHost = options.hostContext;
if (resolveHost === undefined) throw unconfigured("database");     // BEFORE identity — nothing composed
const identity = migrationCommandIdentity(input, projectId);
const host = resolveHost(identity.environment);                    // per-request, admitted environment
const databaseUrl = host?.databaseUrl ?? "", workspace = host?.workspace ?? "";
const projectRoot = host?.projectRoot ?? "";
if (databaseUrl.length === 0 || workspace.length === 0 || projectRoot.length === 0) {
  throw unconfigured(databaseUrl.length === 0
    ? "database" : workspace.length === 0 ? "workspace" : "project root");
}
```
- **ABSENT** refuses exactly where it refuses today — before target admission — so the :95-101 rationale is untouched and byte-identical in effect (today all-three-empty also picks the "database" field for the message; so does the absent branch).
- **NULL / EMPTY FIELD** refuses after identity, which is correct: on a daemon that IS composed, a bad target or payload is the true first fault and `migrationCommandIdentity` should answer it. This is a behaviour DIFFERENCE only for a case that cannot occur today (there is no configured-and-then-null state at HEAD), so nothing regresses.
- **Still ahead of every engine read and write.** `migrationCommandIdentity(input, projectId)` takes NO store (`migrate-down-admission.ts:21`) — pure envelope/principal validation. The first store touch remains `migrationCommandHistory(store, identity)` on the next line, and `revertLastBatch` is far below. DoD 2's "before engine reads or writes" holds for all three refusal arms.

REFUSAL PRESERVED EXACTLY. Same code `MIGRATE_DOWN_UNCONFIGURED`, same layer `DAEMON_COMMAND_SEAM`, same status 422, same per-field message `no <database|workspace|project root> is configured on this daemon`. Factored into one module-private helper `unconfigured(field)` that RETURNS a `DomainRefusal` for the caller to `throw` (returning rather than throwing keeps TypeScript's control-flow narrowing of `resolveHost` honest without an assertion signature). Its doc comment states the secrecy invariant at the point it is enforced: **the message names the FIELD, never the value** — no resolved database URL can reach a refusal string (epic rail 3).

(a) **TWO ENVIRONMENTS PROVE ISOLATION** (DoD 1). Dispatch a real migrate_down naming environment A and assert the revert reached A's database and workspace; dispatch naming environment B and assert it reached B's.
